patterns.name: AI chips are now a national security fight
patterns.line: US lawmakers have summoned Huang and Lutnick, and a Chinese firm tied to Alice Huang reportedly got banned H800 servers. If the hearings and chip-tracking bills advance, export controls will tighten, including in Southeast Asia.

patterns.name: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing
patterns.line: India banned black mass exports to feed its own recyclers, and the IEA says renewables avoided over $100 billion in fuel imports. Solar capacity now outruns demand, so weaker makers face consolidation.

patterns.name: AI is now solving research-level maths problems
patterns.line: An AI model proved a 2011 quantum-computing conjecture in about four days, and Scientific American reports AI moving from maths towards physics. Maths has proof checkers; most sciences lack them, which limits the spread.

patterns.name: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons
patterns.line: Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones in one night, India's Army plans 540 jet-powered kamikaze drones, and UFORCE raised $700M at a $6B valuation. Battlefield results are pulling in both procurement and private money.

patterns.name: India is tightening scrutiny of where AI data goes
patterns.line: MeitY is questioning home-services firms over footage sent to foreign AI developers, while OpenAI adds in-India processing for its APIs. Residency is becoming a condition for selling AI to Indian firms.

money.line: Bengaluru startup automating customer servicing, collections and compliance for banks, NBFCs and insurers; led by Prime Venture Partners, with Invention Engine.
Europe's most valuable robotics startup at $8.5B valuation; round led by SoftBank, with Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital. Total funding about $2B.

lead.headline: Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO after second affair
lead.hook: Jensen Huang ==resigned as Nvidia CEO== after The New York Times exposed a second affair, days after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
points: The second affair was with one of Huang's direct reports. The two scandals landing together made his position untenable; EE Times says he might have survived either alone.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and was CEO for all 33 years. The company is worth around $4 trillion, largely because of AI.
He ran Nvidia with about 42,000 staff; Intel has roughly double that.
Nvidia has only ever had one CEO and no obvious internal successor. The board says it is considering internal and external candidates.
signal: If the board picks an outsider, expect strategy to be judged afresh, since Huang's personal brand and Nvidia's brand are tightly fused.
Separately today, US lawmakers summoned Huang to testify, so the story moves from personnel to policy.
lead.editors_read: A founder-CEO exit is a governance shock for the firm that sells most AI chips. The bigger consequence is political: with a suspected spy in the story, Nvidia loses its main defender in Washington while chip-export enforcement gains momentum. Customers buying GPUs in volume will watch whether the product roadmap changes under a new leader.
lead.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: India's October trade deficit hits a 12-month high on record imports
frontpage.hook: India's trade deficit widened to a 12-month high of $39.88 billion in October as imports hit a record $89.35 billion; exports also hit a record $49.47 billion, up 45%.
points: The deficit is still below last October's $42.58 billion, when imports were $76.69 billion. The rise in imports is likely seasonal.
April-October goods exports were $309.06 billion, up nearly 22%; imports were $527.21 billion, up 16%. The seven-month deficit is $218.15 billion.
Services exports were an estimated $40.51 billion, up 15%; services imports were $20.72 billion, giving a services surplus of $19.79 billion.
Exports reached 14% of GDP in Q1 FY27, up from 11.3% in FY26, 11.7% in FY25 and 12.5% in FY24. US tariffs hit FY26.
The government's target is $1 trillion in total exports, goods plus services, this financial year.
signal: If export growth holds near these rates, the $1 trillion target looks reachable.
frontpage.editors_read: Exports recovering to 14% of GDP, the FY23 level, suggests the US tariff hit is being absorbed. A record import bill alongside record exports usually means firms are buying inputs to re-export. The pressure point is how long imports stay above exports.

frontpage.headline: Russia says it downed nearly 1,200 Ukrainian drones overnight
frontpage.hook: Russia said it shot down 1,198 Ukrainian drones over more than 15 regions overnight, one of Kyiv's largest swarms, and at least four people died in Volgograd.
points: The four dead worked in an industrial zone with an oil refinery and a chemical factory in the southern Volgograd region.
The attack followed US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meeting Putin in Moscow, then Zelensky in Dublin, on peace talks.
On Thursday Russia sent waves of explosive drones at Kyiv, killing at least one person.
Ukraine has intensified drone strikes on Russian energy over 18 months to cut Kremlin revenue and its ability to finance the war.
Ukraine says Russia targets its grid, leaving residents without power as temperatures fall before winter.
signal: Strikes on refineries cost Russia revenue; if swarms of this size repeat, air-defence stocks and energy exports are both strained.
frontpage.editors_read: Ukraine is using cheap drones to attack Russia's income, not just its army. Launching a record swarm just after US envoys left Moscow suggests Kyiv wants leverage before any deal. Both sides now hit energy, so winter becomes a bargaining factor.
frontpage.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

frontpage.headline: AI proves a 2011 quantum computing conjecture
frontpage.hook: Researchers used Anthropic's Fable 5.2 model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, which says quantum computers cannot beat ordinary ones on a class of random-input problems; the model took about four days.
points: The conjecture was set by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis in 2011. Ambainis says he had given up on it.
David Turturean of start-up Physical Superintelligence led the team. The model refined the proof twice, then Lean proof-checking software verified it.
Stanford researchers studied it and call it substantially more difficult than prior work, woven together in a novel way.
It rules out one place to look for quantum speed-ups, but Aaronson says it was not a plausible direction anyway.
Quantum advantage may remain for shorter or less random inputs, molecule simulation and some optimisation problems.
signal: Lean-style verification is what lets AI proofs be trusted; fields without a verifier will move slower.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI is now solving research-level maths problems

frontpage.headline: MeitY questions Pronto and rivals on home footage sent abroad for robot training
frontpage.hook: MeitY asked Pronto, Urban Company and Snabbit whether footage recorded inside Indian homes is sold or sent to physical-AI developers abroad, at a meeting on November 12.
points: Pronto workers wear cameras while doing chores, and the footage trains AI for robots. Pronto has been asked to submit its data practices.
In May Pronto said it deleted footage within 48 hours; in November it said anonymised footage is kept for AI training, without naming who trains on it.
Founder Anjali Sardana launched US-based Provision Labs in October, a physical-AI data collector. Pronto declined to explain how the two work together.
Urban Company and Snabbit say they do not record inside homes.
The DPDP Act allows sending personal data abroad unless a country is restricted, and none is. Transfer conditions take effect only in May 2027.
signal: Until May 2027 no Indian law specifically stops this; if executives' calls to regulate sales succeed, consent for onward sale becomes the key rule.
frontpage.evidence_of: India is tightening scrutiny of where AI data goes

frontpage.headline: Firm founded by Alice Huang got banned Nvidia chips, Bloomberg reports
frontpage.hook: Bloomberg reports that Shanghai Longteng, a company founded by alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, obtained servers with Nvidia H800 chips, which the US banned for export to China in 2023.
points: Singapore-based Nvidia partner Aperia Cloud Services bought the servers from Dell; documents filed with the Chinese government show them later with Shanghai Longteng.
It is unclear how the hardware was obtained or whether Alice Huang was involved.
She is mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore data-centre firm under scrutiny for allegedly steering Nvidia chips to China.
Megaspeed says it is investigating its export-control compliance; Malaysia is probing a Megaspeed subsidiary.
China denies she is a spy.
signal: If diversion is confirmed through an official partner, pressure grows on Nvidia and its resellers to prove where chips end up.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: OpenAI adds India-only processing for its API
frontpage.hook: OpenAI launched local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, initially for GPT-6 Luna, so both requests and compute stay in the country.
points: Customers create a new API project, choose India for storage and processing, and use the India regional endpoint.
India joins Australia and Japan as markets with API inference residency.
Banks, financial institutions and government agencies often cannot use foreign frontier models if data leaves the country, OpenAI says.
Anthropic announced in-country inference for Claude via Amazon Bedrock in August. This could narrow the local-hosting edge of startups like Sarvam AI.
More than 10 Cr people use ChatGPT weekly in India, OpenAI's largest market, and it is looking to monetise it.
signal: If regulated firms can now buy frontier models with data kept in India, enterprise adoption in banking and government may speed up.
frontpage.evidence_of: India is tightening scrutiny of where AI data goes

frontpage.headline: Indian Army plans 540 jet-powered kamikaze drones
frontpage.hook: The Indian Army begins field trials this week at Pokhran for 540 jet-powered kamikaze drones in a roughly Rs 2,000 crore programme, its first dedicated buy of such weapons.
points: Of about 60 firms that responded to the July RFI, 18 bid and 11 qualified. Only Indian companies can compete, and they must supply vehicles and mission-planning support too.
Jet-powered loitering munitions fly at around 450 kmph versus 150-200 kmph for propeller types, so they arrive sooner and are harder to intercept.
DRDO's GTRE has developed a 350 kg class expendable turbojet, working with Azad Engineering.
The Army has already received 106 Agniveg jet drones from SMPP, flying up to 450 kmph.
Russia's Geran-4 flies at 450-500 kmph, and Ukrainian intelligence estimates Russia makes about 3,000 Geran-4 and Geran-5 a month.
signal: If trials pass, Indian engine and drone makers get an assured buyer; Fast Track Procurement implies quick orders.
frontpage.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

frontpage.headline: India says TB deaths fell 38%, treatment success 94%
frontpage.hook: India's Health Ministry says TB mortality fell 38% and 94% of drug-susceptible patients were successfully treated, after WHO's report found India reached a 35% mortality reduction in 2025.
points: The Ministry credits proactive case finding, AI-enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment and nutrition support.
Between December 7, 2024 and November 8, 2026, over 25 crore people were screened under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.
That drive produced over 11 crore chest X-rays and more than 3 crore NAAT tests (molecular diagnostic tests).
It found 48.64 lakh new cases, including 14.97 lakh with no symptoms.
signal: Finding asymptomatic cases, about 31% of those identified, is where portable AI X-rays add most.

stories.headline: Nvidia privately said chip tracking is possible, despite industry objections
stories.hook: Nvidia representatives privately told Rep. Bill Foster that the Chip Security Act's anti-smuggling tracking is technically possible, while an industry group called it "potentially infeasible".
points: The act, cosponsored by Foster, would require geotracking to verify advanced AI chips' locations. It is one of three chip-security bills considered for the Senate's defence bill.
In March 2026 the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, called the mandates "new, untested, and potentially infeasible".
Foster says Nvidia put nothing in writing; Nvidia did not respond. Its Fleet Intelligence tool, announced December 2025, can indicate which country chips are in.
The ping-based option, where a GPU reports its location when it powers on, is hardest to circumvent and most cost-effective, a September CSET study found.
Tracking shows where chips are but cannot disable them. Foster plans stricter legislation in the new year requiring licences to operate advanced GPUs.
signal: If the tracking passes with the defence bill, firms must prove chip locations; licence-to-operate rules would follow.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

stories.headline: US Senate summons Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify
stories.hook: The Senate Banking Committee has asked Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify on December 3, threatening subpoenas if they refuse.
points: Three House committees separately asked Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter to appear on December 1 and 2. Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler was summoned for December 3.
Nvidia's market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.
The Trump administration faces allegations that Nvidia exports to China were not properly scrutinised, and that Commerce refused to blacklist dozens of Chinese firms.
China warned that tighter US chip export rules threaten global supply chains; lawmakers also want limits on chip-equipment exports.
Trump earlier called Huang "honourable".
signal: Hearings put the administration's own export enforcement under scrutiny, not only Nvidia.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

stories.headline: Microsoft 365 outage knocks out Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide
stories.hook: A Microsoft 365 outage that began Thursday still disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot into Friday, with Outlook problem reports peaking at 138,058 on Downdetector.
points: Microsoft says a core process on affected servers was overwhelmed, so servers stopped responding. Remaining servers took the extra load, and its first recovery steps did not hold.
It says there is no sign of a cyberattack, and the cause was fewer servers available rather than more traffic. It extended the email timeout window to 48 hours.
Traders in Asia fell back on phones, WhatsApp and fax; trade confirmations backed up and Japan's Finance Ministry could not receive email.
IndiGo and Akasa Air email support was hit; Air India rerouted email. Workhorse Group postponed earnings from November 12 to November 16.
OpenAI and Anthropic said their Microsoft 365 connectors were affected.
signal: Counterpoint's Tarun Pathak says Outlook and Teams are core operational infrastructure; India's IT firms, BPOs and GCCs are exposed, so continuity plans are likely to be reviewed.
Separately today, Microsoft cited a second outage in weeks (Azure last month), so single-vendor dependence is a live question.

also.line: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue vowed to keep backing open-source AI after Huang's exit; Nvidia's $12.9 billion purchase is due to close in H1 2027 and faces a DOJ inquiry.

stories.headline: SMIC: AI chip supply to stay tight through 2027
stories.hook: China's largest contract chipmaker SMIC says supply of AI-related chips stays tight through 2027, with memory supply and demand balancing only around mid-to-late 2028.
points: Co-CEO Zhao Haijun, asked about an AI bubble, said the industry is early-stage and many customers still face compute shortages.
Demand comes from data centres and private clouds.
Equipment orders sometimes take more than 24 months to deliver, which affects capital spending.
SMIC expects full-year revenue above $1.2 billion as capacity use rises, and 2026 depreciation expense up about 30%.
signal: If equipment waits stay above 24 months, new chip capacity cannot arrive before the 2027 tightness ends.
stories.evidence_of: AI chip demand is outrunning supply

also.line: Bloomberg Economics says Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy tied to firms in Singapore and Malaysia raises the risk of tighter US chip export rules that could stall Southeast Asia's AI boom.
ASUS is developing a humanoid robot, Gallop, for repetitive electronics-factory tasks; customer pilots are planned for 2027 and commercial availability targeted for the second half of 2028.

stories.headline: India's road-fuel demand to keep rising until 2034 despite EVs
stories.hook: India's road-fuel demand will peak at more than 2.5 million barrels a day in 2034, eight years away, before falling, BloombergNEF's EV outlook says (summary from limited source text).
points: A growing vehicle fleet and heavier commercial transport use sustain oil demand.
Rising adoption of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and cars should eventually outweigh commercial-vehicle growth and push demand lower.
signal: Oil import needs keep growing for eight years, so EV adoption alone does not cut near-term import dependence.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India bans battery black mass exports to feed domestic recyclers
stories.hook: India banned exports of battery scrap including black mass, with immediate effect, moving it from 'Free' to 'Prohibited', because it is 100% import-dependent for lithium, nickel and cobalt.
points: Black mass is powder from shredded lithium-ion batteries containing lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese.
Twelve Indian units process black mass, with 75,500 tonnes a year of input capacity, but lack enough feedstock. Commerce says some recyclers imported black mass while local material was exported.
Black-mass-only recyclers may see lower prices as export buyers go. Enforcement is a risk: exporters could declare it as cobalt powder or nickel intermediates.
From FY28, battery makers must use minimum quantities of domestically recycled material in new batteries.
Recyclers say much battery waste is informal, and a shift to LFP batteries, with little nickel or cobalt, lowers feedstock value.
signal: If customs enforce it, domestic refiners get the feedstock; value then depends on India building cathode-material makers.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India's solar makers face consolidation as supply outruns demand
stories.hook: India has about 225 GW of module capacity against annual solar installations of 40-45 GW, and GREW Solar's Hiten Parekh expects aggressive pricing and consolidation to 20-25 major makers.
points: Cell capacity is 38 GW. Parekh expects very aggressive pricing for two to three quarters, after which weaker makers struggle and prices normalise.
Input costs are up: some raw materials about 2.5 times pre-February levels, and cell prices at least 1.5 times higher in six months, squeezing margins.
Uncertainty over whether ALMM List II provisions extend beyond December complicates buying; developers are contracting six to eight months ahead.
US Section 232 barriers and anti-dumping duties have effectively closed direct module exports to the US.
GREW has 3.5 GW of cell capacity, plans 9 GW, and an 8 GW wafer facility in Madhya Pradesh targeted for 2027-2028.
signal: Survivors will be those that integrate upstream into wafers and have strong balance sheets.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: Renewables saved India over $100 billion in fuel imports, IEA says
stories.hook: India avoided more than $100 billion (Rs 9.4 lakh crore) in coal and gas import costs from 2011 to 2025 through renewables, the IEA's India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026 estimates.
points: Without renewable capacity added since 2010, India would have imported about 110 million tonnes more coal in 2025, and electricity import dependence would have been above 30%, nearly twice the actual level.
Renewable capacity crossed 300 GW in 2026; 50% of installed capacity was non-fossil in 2025, five years ahead of target.
Renewables made over 500 TWh in 2025, one-fourth of supply; the IEA projects about 950 TWh, 35%, by 2030.
Solar costs $30-35 per MWh, and 2025 project tariffs were about 40% below the average cost of coal power.
Gas import dependence is projected to rise from 52% in 2024 to about 71% by 2030.
__Cumulative savings could reach about $240 billion by 2030__, assuming fuel prices stay near 2024-25 averages.
signal: Faster transmission, storage and discom finances could lift 2026-30 capacity additions by more than 20%.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

also.line: PM Surya Ghar, India's main rooftop solar scheme, has reached 67% of its target and is nearing 20 GW, with ₹374.07 billion in subsidies disbursed so far.

stories.headline: FDA's 2026 warning letters hit Asia hard, BioSpectrum finds
stories.hook: The US FDA posted 513 warning letters between 13 January and 10 November 2026; 59 went to Asia-Pacific firms, 25 to India and 22 to China.
points: Of 121 letters on drug manufacturing quality, 45 went to sites in the region.
The median drug quality letter appeared on fda.gov eight days after it was issued, often before the company's reply was due.
FDA enforced in coordinated waves, such as compounded GLP-1 marketing and talc products, and import alerts often come before the letter.
BioSpectrum's whitepaper covers cases including Reliance Life Sciences, Eugia, Intas, Zydus and Dabur.
signal: Public letters within days mean quality gaps become headlines before firms can respond; Indian exporters need records ready.

also.line: STAT's health-tech newsletter reports new documents raising more questions about Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Study: the monsoon's large-scale onset starts in Northeast India around May 15
stories.hook: An IIT-Madras and Gauhati University study of 84 years of rainfall data finds the large-scale monsoon system forms over Northeast India around May 15, nearly three weeks before it is established over the peninsula.
points: Clusters of rainfall onset form independently, including in Northeast India from April. Around May 15 the Northeast cluster merges with a system from the southeastern Bay of Bengal.
Around June 9, the Northeast and peninsular clusters merge over the peninsula, which marks the large-scale monsoon.
The large-scale rainy season in Northeast India and the southwest peninsula is 20-30 days shorter than the locally defined season.
Large-scale withdrawal begins over Northwest India around September 22 and covers much of the country by October 22.
Applied to 2026, the method flagged June 22 as large-scale onset over the peninsula; Mumbai got heavy rain on June 24.
signal: If the method works live, farmers could avoid sowing on false onsets, but the authors say it complements official definitions.

stories.headline: Zupee's AI pivot was cover for a shutdown, Inc42 reports
stories.hook: Gaming startup Zupee has laid off its entire workforce, and sources say its October 16 AI pivot announcement masked an impending closure.
points: Severance covers the period to January 2027. Only 3-4 people remain working with the founders, sources say; Zupee did not respond.
Two earlier rounds cut about 170 and about 200 employees; headcount peaked near 500.
The real-money gaming ban hit its revenue, and casual games could not replace it.
It also shut astrology platform NeoAstro and microdrama venture Zupee Studio; the Vertical TV acquisition fell through.
It raised over $120 million from investors including Z47, Orios and WestCap. None responded to Inc42 on recovering capital.
signal: Remaining cash and liabilities are unknown; investors' recovery depends on a wind-down process not yet disclosed.
stories.evidence_of: India is tightening rules on online money

stories.headline: Paytm gets preliminary RBI nod for a wallet licence
stories.hook: Paytm's payments services unit received preliminary RBI approval to issue prepaid payment products including wallets, sending shares to a record high of ₹1,960.
points: Final RBI authorisation is still needed before wallets can be offered.
It comes over two years after the RBI barred Paytm Payments Bank from taking fresh deposits and wallet top-ups over persistent non-compliance.
The RBI cancelled the Payments Bank's banking licence earlier this year.
The wholly owned subsidiary can now move towards restarting wallet services.
signal: If final approval comes, Paytm regains a product halted since the ban.

stories.headline: India funds deeptech, but who will buy what it builds?
stories.hook: Agnikul Cosmos received Rs 200 crore from the RDI Fund to build a reusable launch vehicle, but The CapTable says the government has no matching buyer (summary from limited source text).
points: The Government of India has built a large pipeline of deeptech funding.
The missing piece is demand inside the system for the technology being funded.
signal: Without government purchase commitments, funded startups may lack first customers.

stories.headline: Ukrainian defence startup UFORCE raised $700M at a $6B valuation
stories.hook: UFORCE raised $700 million at a $6 billion valuation, up from about $1 billion in March when it raised $50 million.
points: Valor Equity Partners and the UK's National Wealth Fund co-led the Series A.
The CEO says bookings more than doubled in a year from a base of several hundred million dollars; he gave no exact figures.
It makes unmanned air, sea and land systems plus AI to coordinate them; it says NEMESIS drones have flown over 300,000 combat flights.
Funds will scale manufacturing in Ukraine and allied countries; the CEO says Ukrainian needs come first.
Startups across NATO and allied countries raised $27.1 billion through September, nearly double all of 2025.
signal: If bookings growth holds, the valuation rests on proven combat use; customers remain undisclosed.
stories.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

stories.headline: Shield AI opens Bengaluru engineering office for Indian defence autonomy
stories.hook: US firm Shield AI opened a Bengaluru engineering office, its second in India after New Delhi in April 2026, to build autonomy software for Indian aircraft and defence systems.
points: The office focuses on Hivemind, its software for developing and operating autonomous systems, and will hire autonomy, flight-software and simulation engineers.
Hivemind has been piloted across more than 40 platforms, including F-16s, helicopters, uncrewed vessels and a satellite.
JSW Group committed $90 million to make Shield AI's V-BAT drone in India; construction began in December 2025 in Hyderabad.
In January 2026 Shield AI was selected to supply V-BAT aircraft and Hivemind licences to the Indian Army.
signal: Local engineering suggests foreign defence-tech firms are building teams in India, not only selling.
stories.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

stories.headline: Megaspeed's global footprint is thin, odd and obscure, Guardian finds
stories.hook: Megaspeed International, which bought nearly $5 billion in Nvidia chips and hardware in three years, has offices that reporters found nearly empty or unaware of it.
points: Its Australian affiliate lists a Shanghai-born director, 29-year-old Kai Kang, with a Victoria lottery shop as home address; his mother says he knows nothing of the Singapore firm. Kang is not accused of wrongdoing.
Singapore held Alice Huang's passport from June 2025 until February over potential false declarations, and barred her from re-entering. Taiwan also barred her.
Malaysia is investigating a Megaspeed subsidiary over possible diversion of AI chips.
Experts say it would be credible to assess it as a front for Chinese intelligence, but nothing is certain. China calls the claims smears.
signal: Shell-like affiliates across Asia explain why tracing chips after sale is hard.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

stories.headline: Euclid's first major data release maps 900 million galaxies
stories.hook: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission released data covering over 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 probable strong gravitational lenses, up from about 1,000 known before.
points: The release covers about 14% of the sky area Euclid will map; it also includes more than 60 million potential quasars.
Strong lensing, where a foreground galaxy bends light from a distant one, shows how dark matter clumps, which can rule out theories of what it is.
Dark energy and dark matter are thought to make up about 70% and 25% of the universe.
About 170,000 lenses are expected by mission end; the next release, next summer, adds weak-lensing results to map dark matter.
The data is now too big for humans to examine by eye.
signal: Lens counts rising from about 1,000 to 15,000 give dark-matter theories far more data to be tested against.

stories.headline: AI has upended maths; Scientific American asks if science is next
stories.hook: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated preprints on about 370 open problems in October, as scientists debate whether AI discoveries can spread beyond maths.
points: In May OpenAI models, guided by humans, disproved an Erdős conjecture; in August AI models effectively solved the Navier-Stokes problem, amid controversy.
Maths has verifiers such as Lean; most sciences have none, so AI claims are harder to check.
Harvard's Matthew Schwartz released 36 preprints across 22 areas but says he can't name a deep insight in physics yet. In one case an expert refuted a claimed 15% earthquake-forecasting gain.
Others doubt it: physical chemist Leslie Schoop says models could not find a structure her lab discovered, and neuroscientist Mark Histed says neuroscience needs better data, not more intelligence.
signal: Fields with checkable answers and plentiful data go first; lab and measurement work is shielded for now.
stories.evidence_of: AI is now solving research-level maths problems

stories.headline: AI improves brain-implant stimulation for a blind man
stories.hook: A deep-learning model picked electrical stimulation patterns for a 96-electrode visual-cortex implant, producing intended brain activity more accurately than comparison methods with less current.
points: The participant is a 27-year-old man blinded by traumatic brain injury, tested at Hospital IMED Elche in Spain. The implant was to stay in six months.
The AI predicted cortical responses using stimulation settings plus resting brain activity just before stimulation.
Recorded brain activity predicted what he perceived better than stimulation settings did.
Perception was limited to flashes and shapes of light. The study, in Neuron, is proof of concept from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich and Miguel Hernández University.
signal: Implants may need to adapt to each brain; this is early research, not a product.

also.line: A Scientific American podcast episode describes stuttering as a neurologic disorder affecting timing, initiation and flow of speech (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Moody's: no clear sign yet of AI hitting Indian IT jobs
stories.hook: Moody's says AI's impact on jobs and productivity is not yet clearly visible in India, even though India and the Philippines are the emerging markets most exposed through IT and BPO.
points: AI could both raise productivity and displace jobs in software, IT and BPO-heavy economies.
Access to computing power, digital infrastructure and skilled workers will decide how much countries gain.
Moody's raised India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7% from 6.5%.
For China and India, higher interest payments are expected to add more to public debt than budget deficits.
Its sovereign outlook lists weaker-than-expected AI investment returns as a key risk.
signal: Absence of evidence now doesn't mean none later; compute and skills are the constraints to watch.
stories.evidence_of: AI lets firms grow revenue with fewer hires

also.line: Saregama says it uses AI to cut costs and improve efficiency, and to create content and track unauthorised covers, while vowing action against unlicensed use of its music catalogue.
The Guardian's Ammar Kalia names Sheherazaad's album Khudgarzi his global album of the month; she debuted with the EP Qasr in 2024 (summary from limited source text).

opportunities.name: One Human, Ten AI Agents
opportunities.when: Sun 29 Nov; registration requests reviewed after 17 November
opportunities.summary: Talk plus hands-on workshop by Cluster on agentic AI: build and run a small team of AI agents live. Open to students, requires host approval, New Delhi.

opportunities.name: CSAIC Hack-AI-Thon
opportunities.summary: Five-day online AI hackathon for school students across India; teams of 1-3 build projects in tracks including AI for Education and AI for Environment (summary from limited source text).
